note: THE category-exclude LIBRARY - single source of truth for wrong-class product tokens. Three consumers: (1) audit-food-category.ps1 (blocking guard: a food commodity matched to one of these classes hard-fails the publish), (2) apply-category-excludes.ps1 (bakes these patterns into every commodity's exclude list by category, so NEW commodities are born with the guardrails), (3) build-vet-sheet.ps1 (flags them for batch review). Born from the 2026-07-14 blueberries-as-Bai-beverage live mispricing. RULE FOR ADDING PATTERNS: a token belongs here ONLY if it is wrong for EVERY commodity in the scoped categories (after exempt); anything item-specific stays in that commodity's own exclude list. frozen_dessert_brand (2026-08-30, queue 2026-08-30-2611d3) is the first BRAND class: Blue Bunny crowned Family Fare pistachios at $0.1248/oz with a 48 oz tub of ice cream, and every type-word fence missed it because the retail name carries only BRAND + FLAVOR (no ice cream, no dessert, no frozen). A brand token only belongs here when every product the brand sells is the wrong class: all 40 Blue Bunny strings in out/ are frozen desserts, and the exempt regex carries the commodities a Blue Bunny product legitimately IS. sausage_carrier (2026-09-02, queue 2026-09-02-1527d2) is the first CARRIER-FORM class: a chicken sausage flavoured with gruyere held the Family Fare gruyere cell at $0.5825/oz, and nothing in a library of brand and type words could say that a product is a sausage which lists the food as a flavour. Measured the same day over 33,854 corpus names: 455 carry sausage(s) and 25 of those route to 15 commodities that are not sausage (apples five times over), a gap that had been closed one per-product ruling at a time since 2026-08-01. The exempt regex carries the 21 ids that ARE a sausage or legitimately contain one; a sausage is the wrong product for every other commodity in the scoped categories, which is what makes this a library class rather than 15 separate excludes. cheese_carrier and cracker_carrier (2026-09-04, queue 2026-09-04-2cd17a, triage-plans\plan-2026-09-04.json) are the same shape one category further out: Aldi's 'Emporium Selection Bacon Bread Cheese 6 OZ' (a baked CHEESE) routed to bacon and its Original sibling to bread, and 'Savoritz Sea Salt Sourdough Pita Cracker 5 OZ' routed to pita-bread because that commodity's hand-written exclude carried the literal plural 'crackers' and the singular walked past it - the library already had the \bcrackers?\b form in snack_carrier but no bake scope reached Bread & Bakery. Bread & Bakery gets its own apply block for that reason (it previously shared the Dairy/Canned/... block and therefore could not gain a class the others must not have). steam_bag_carrier (2026-09-08, queue 2026-09-08-2e59b3, triage-plans\plan-2026-09-08.json) is the first FORM class carried only by a BRAND LINE: the frozen microwave steam bag. Fresh per-lb and per-each produce commodities refuse a form by literal word (\bfrozen\b on 25 of the 98 lb commodities, \bsteam\b on 3), but Green Giant Steamers, Birds Eye Steamfresh, Green Giant SteamCrisp, Fareway/Season's Choice/Our Family/Simple Truth Steamable(s) and Birds Eye's Sauced line carry no form word at all, so any such bag whose name contains the produce word is eligible for the FRESH commodity, wins on array index, and is kept off the cell only while a sanity band censors it or a cheaper fresh row shadows it. Measured over 19,099 corpus names (plan-2026-09-08.routing.json): 66 names carry a steam-bag word and 7 change route; 'Fareway Steamables Green Beans', a frozen 12 oz bag, was holding Fareway's LIVE fresh-green-beans cell at $1.92 per lb over the fresh Pero row at $2.94. Scoped to Fruit and Vegetables only, because the shared Dairy/Canned/... apply block also covers Frozen, whose commodities MUST keep these names; the two canned ids that the same names fall into (canned-green-beans, canned-peas) carry the tokens in their own exclude lists instead. Deliberately NOT tokens: \bsteamcrisp\b on the canned ids (Green Giant SteamCrisp White Shoepeg is a real can at canned-corn) and 'steams? in bag' anywhere (Kroger Steams in Bag Petite Carrots is FRESH produce, in band at carrots, and must keep routing there). soup_carrier and sushi_carrier (2026-09-11, queue 2026-09-11-3b246c, triage-plans\plan-2026-09-11.json) are the first PREPARED-DISH carrier classes: a raw-protein commodity includes its bare name, so a soup, chowder, bisque or sushi roll named for its protein is eligible at every Meat commodity and only a price band sees the cheap ones. Sam's 'Member's Mark Shrimp and Corn Chowder, 24 oz., 2 pk.' ($10.47 / 3 lb = $3.49/lb, exact arithmetic) took the shrimp crown from real raw shrimp at $5.82/lb, and Aldi's shrimp cell was 'Fusia Shrimp Avocado Roll Sushi 11.5 OZ'. Measured over 22,713 corpus names (plan-2026-09-11.routing.json): baked into ^Meat the two classes move 2 names (exactly those rows); into ^(Fruit|Vegetables)$ they move 1 ('Fresh & Finest Herbed Tomato Bisque' tomatoes -> tomato-soup, a correct re-landing). Exempt is empty because no commodity in either block is a soup or a sushi; canned-chili, clam-chowder and tomato-soup sit in other blocks. Extended later on 2026-09-11 (queue 2026-09-10-fa6ad6): once Family Fare's whole 1,045-row circular reached the board, ad rows that carry no shelf path put Nutri Grain Breakfast Bars on raspberries, strawberries and cherries and Cascade dishwasher pacs ('Cascade Ap Comp Lemon') on lemons, none with a type word any class knew. snack_carrier gains breakfast bars, Nutri-Grain and cereal bars; household gains cascade (Cascadian Farm does not match the word). Measured with the commodity fences shipped beside them over 1,337 corpus names carrying a proposed token: 20 routing changes, every one a wrong product or a frozen meal. condiment_carrier (2026-09-19, design\PLAN-board-accuracy-2026-09-19.md 4f) is the CONDIMENT shape of the same disease: a blind verification of 100 board cells found Aldi's 'Burman S Green Chili Squeeze Aioli 10 OZ' priced as fresh green-chilli, because canned-green-chilies and mayonnaise each fenced aioli by hand and green-chilli never did. The class names the condiment forms (aioli, squeeze, mayo/mayonnaise, dip, dressing, spread), is scoped where the other produce carriers are, and reaches 114 of the 116 Fruit and Vegetables commodities; the exempt carries the two whose own products ARE a squeeze paste or carry a dressing (lemongrass-paste, caesar-salad-kit). Measured over the 43,309 distinct names the 2026-09-17 board read (90 input files): 13 produce names left a produce cell, every one a dressing, spread, squeeze or aioli, and three of them first re-landed on sea-salt, ranch-dressing and mayonnaise until those were fenced in the same change. soup_carrier's \bstews?\b and canned_carrier (2026-09-19, Brad's ruling 'fence stews and cans off produce', design\ready-for-brad\produce-condiment-exclusion.md): Walmart's 'Stokes Green Chile Stew with Pork and Potatoes, Medium, 15 oz Can' was the cheapest green-chilli cell because the fresh fence had \bcanned\b and not the word Can, and soup_carrier had no stew. Stew is a soup-shaped prepared dish and goes in soup_carrier (Meat as well; it moved only stews there, and no stew-meat product routes to any Meat commodity today). The can word is its OWN class scoped to Fruit and Vegetables only, because in soup_carrier it reached Meat, where canned-tuna, canned-chicken, canned-salmon and diced-ham price real cans and a fresh Hormel pork shoulder ad reads 'TASTE WHAT PORK CAN DO': measured over 77,482 distinct names (every item/product/name string under grocery\out plus the 2026-09-17 board corpus), the can word in soup_carrier moved 198 names, most of them real canned meat leaving its own cell; produce-only, the two tokens moved 70, every one a canned, freeze-dried, drink, seed, recipe-title or stew product leaving a fresh produce or Meat cell, 27 of them in the board corpus. Two board-corpus re-landings were fenced in the same change (canned-peas: carrots; dried-oregano: tomato paste); four names outside the board corpus still re-land on another wrong commodity (chickpeas, ramen, frozen-corn, rice) and are listed in that document.

apply.note: Bread & Bakery used to fall into the shared Dairy/Canned/Sauces/... block below and therefore could not be given a class the others must not have. This block MUST stay above that one: apply-category-excludes.ps1:34 takes the FIRST block whose regex matches the category label, so a block appended after the shared one would be unreachable (the first-match-wins trap that left dried_carrier baked into 0 of 83 vegetables). Its first eight classes are exactly the shared block's; the last two are what Bread gains.

dried/flake spice-jar forms are wrong for every FRESH-produce commodity, but Fruit is excluded from scope on purpose: dried-cranberries and raisins are Fruit rows whose own products carry the word dried. Born from the 2026-08-20 contested review: Dan's Pantry Rosemary, Gourmet Garden basil paste, freeze-dried red onion and McCormick celery flakes were all pricing fresh rows.

apply_ids.note: ID-SCOPED CLASSES (2026-09-18, queue 2026-09-18-f90ba6, triage-plans\plan-2026-09-18.json). The apply blocks above scope a class by the deals page's DISPLAY category, and a display bucket can mix foods with drinks: pistachios sits in 'Snacks & Drinks' beside soda, coffee pods and iced tea, and peanuts, almonds, walnuts and mixed-nuts sit in 'Coffee, Oils & Spreads' beside coffee, so no category block can ever give a nut the beverage class. A pistachio MILK ('Whole Moon Pistachio Plant Beverage Whole Protein', Baker's, 42 fl oz, $5.99) held the pistachios crown at 0.1426/oz against real nuts at 0.4056 while audit-food-category read OK. A block here is UNIONED into whatever the category pass gave each listed id, by apply-category-excludes.ps1, audit-food-category.ps1 and build-vet-sheet.ps1 alike. It lives under its own key and NOT inside apply because every reader of apply takes the FIRST block whose categories regex matches, and a block with no regex reads as the empty pattern, which matches every label. Measured over 19,416 corpus names (plan-2026-09-18.routing.json variant B2): the five nut ids own 162 names and exactly 1 moves (the beverage, to no commodity). WIDENED 2026-09-18 to all 21 non-drink Snacks & Drinks commodities (queue 2026-09-18-55b7aa, plan-2026-09-18-4.json), and this ids list now carries them. Variant B3 had been REJECTED because the bare gatorade token re-routed two Gatorade protein bars from protein-bars to sports-drinks; the release that unblocked it was to NARROW the beverage class token to a gatorade form with a negative lookahead for protein bar, and to give snack_carrier its own protein-bar token, NOT to drop protein-bars from this list. DO NOT READ THAT REJECTION AS STILL LIVE. Re-measured 2026-09-20 (queue 2026-09-18-f90ba6, plan-2026-09-20-4.json): all 25 ids here carry all 30 beverage tokens in commodities.json, apply-category-excludes.ps1 -WhatIf bakes +0 patterns, all three readers (the bake, audit-food-category, build-vet-sheet) union this block, and comparison-2026-09-20 carries 0 beverage products across their 143 priced cells. That one stale sentence is why this condition returned a third time: plan-2026-09-19 and plan-2026-09-20-2 both carried the claim that apply_ids reaches pistachios only forward from prose the data beside it had already overtaken. Re-measure this list before quoting it.
